description: A function returning {:ok, value, rest} | {:error, reason} allocates a heap tuple per call even when every consumer takes the tuple apart; a one-shape return ({acc, b}) already travels as fields. Probe (scratch cursor/ret.exs): 1,048,576 steps of item(v(b), acc) allocate 1,048,576 tuples plus about 4 continuations per step. In the JSON decoder this is one 48-byte tuple and one binary stub per decoded value, and it is what keeps the returned rest whole after the cursor (fz-sc8.208). Paper-first: a tag lane plus the union of field lanes, or one return entry per shape. Approved for filing by the user 2026-11-14 with the fz-sc8.208 page.

comments.text: Concordant evidence from Make Distiller Fast's BEAM-gap page (https://claude.ai/artifact/4JyVHKjbDBw1bzRDu17PZd): a case value of two tuple shapes passed to a call costs 4 field-read calls and 2 shares per step (1,124 vs 747 instructions per step); {:ok, v, r} structs ≈3.2G of the distiller's JSON decode (with fz-sc8.251).

title: A return of two tuple shapes travels as fields
